task: A new manager asks you what stonewalling is and how to take a time-out instead. Explain it to them in two sentences.
model: Stonewalling means going quiet or pulling away without saying why, so the other person feels ignored. In a time-out you tell them you need a pause, agree when you'll come back, and then come back.

ideas.heading: Stonewalling
ideas.body: Stonewalling is going silent, withdrawing or changing the subject without saying why. The other person feels ignored or rejected. The problem stays unsolved.
ideas.label: Stonewalling is withdrawing without saying why.
ideas.met: You described stonewalling as withdrawing without saying why.
ideas.missed: Say what stonewalling looks like: going silent, withdrawing or changing the subject without saying why.
ideas.unsure: I couldn't tell whether you described stonewalling. Say what it looks like.

ideas.heading: Taking a time-out
ideas.body: A time-out starts when you tell the other person you need a pause. For example, "I need ten minutes to think about this." Stepping away to calm down is fine. Doing it without a word is stonewalling.
ideas.label: A time-out starts by telling the other person you need a pause.
ideas.met: You said a time-out starts by telling the other person you need a pause.
ideas.missed: Add how a time-out starts. You tell the other person you need a pause.
ideas.unsure: I couldn't tell whether you said to announce the pause.

ideas.heading: Coming back
ideas.body: A time-out ends when you come back. Agree when you'll return to the conversation, then do it. That way the other person isn't left waiting.
ideas.label: You agree when to come back, and then come back.
